title: Quantum Anchor Protocol: Frequency-Domain Wave-Packet Encoding with Hardware-Validated Quantum Bridge
description:
Quantum Anchor Protocol encodes a frequency-domain wave packet into quantum interference circuits. This release adds a hardware-validated quantum bridge: the encoding was measured on a real 156-qubit superconducting QPU (IBM ibm_marrakesh, 2000 shots per run, 2026-10-06), reaching 99.3% Bell balance on two qubits, 98.8% on a reproducibility run, and an ideal three-qubit GHZ distribution. The decoding formulas' assumption P(q0=1)=sin^2(theta/2) is therefore measurement-verified rather than assumed.

Tesseract-V3 5-phase interferometric sweep on IQM Garnet (20Q, Starter tier): 5 phases, 1024 shots each (5120 total). Wilson 95% CIs: [0.74, 2.16], [0.10, 0.86], [0.05, 0.71], [0.82, 2.28], [0.10, 0.86] (%). Aggregate: 0.684% [0.49%, 0.95%]. Chi2 vs cos(8φ): 2.99 (df=4), p=0.56 — does NOT reject. Chi2 vs flat: 1.99 (df=4), p=0.74 — does NOT reject. Cos(8φ) fit: offset=0.684%, amplitude=0.514% (theory: 1.56%, 3x smaller), R^2=0.49. Evidence grade: F (Noise-dominated — NO phase discrimination). Pulse-level anchor drive blocked by IQM Starter tier (pulse access denied).

Classical and hardware proofs are reported as strictly separate evidence levels. Negative results reported honestly.
